title: Northern Liang
capsule: Northern Liang was one of the Sixteen Kingdoms of post-Han northern China, established in 397 when Juqu Mengxun overthrew Duan Ye (whom he had initially supported) and seized power in northern Gansu. Juqu Mengxun (r. 401–433) proved an able ruler who expanded control across the entire Hexi Corridor, making Zhangye the capital and fostering Buddhism — the monk Dharmakṣema produced important sūtra translations at the court. The kingdom maintained diplomatic relations with the Northern Wei and with the Liu Song dynasty in the south, balancing between competing powers. Northern Liang fell in 439 when Northern Wei Emperor Taiwu invaded and captured the capital Guzang, extinguishing the last of the Sixteen Kingdoms; a rump Juqu state held out in Turfan until 460.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Northern Liang's territorial extent along the Hexi Corridor is well attested through Chinese dynastic histories; its nomadic frontier boundaries to the north are less precisely defined.
